title: Your Life at Every Level of Getting Sued by a Debt Collector
format: FORMAT_BLUEPRINT – DAC (Your Life at Every Level of …, nivåkort, siffer-bubblor) + DUI-mallen (vanlig händelse i tidsordning)

beats.text: du har aldrig haft med Harborline att göra
du är innanför fönstret – 4 månader kvar
posterna måste anges var för sig
köpta fordringar får inte gå till small claims
regeln du borde ha känt till

scenes.say: Mailbox 14B has never closed right. Tonight an envelope is sticking out of it.
It says you owe 3,812 dollars, and you have 30 days.
This is your life at every level of getting sued by a debt collector, from this envelope to your paycheck.
The sender is Harborline Asset Recovery. You've never heard of them.
Your phone buzzes again. Same 916 number, the eighth call in six days.

visual.text: same 916 number, six days

scenes.say: By the end you'll know what Harborline probably paid for your debt, and the number will make you angry.

visual.text: what the company suing you paid for your debt

scenes.say: Federal law gives a collector five days after first contacting you to send a notice like this, with the amount and the creditor's name.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: to send you the validation notice

scenes.say: Level one. The letter.
At the kitchen counter you read the rest. The original creditor is Copperleaf Bank, a card you cut in half back in 2023.
You remember the card. You don't remember owing anyone named Harborline a single dollar of it.
The notice also starts a clock. You get 30 days after you receive it to dispute the debt, and the rules assume the mail takes five business days.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: to dispute after you receive the notice

scenes.say: If you dispute it in writing inside that window, the collector has to stop collecting until it mails you verification of the debt.

visual.text: a written dispute pauses collection

scenes.say: You put the letter in the kitchen drawer, on top of the takeout menus, and tell yourself you'll call them tomorrow.

note_card.text: 30 DAYS TO DISPUTE IN WRITING (REG F)

scenes.say: Level two. The calls.
Day 9. You're on the loading dock at the warehouse, wrapping pallets, when the 916 number calls for the ninth time.

note_card.text: REG F: 30 DAYS TO DISPUTE AFTER YOU GET THE NOTICE

scenes.say: Your coworker Dante watches you decline it again. He has driven a forklift for 22 years, and he only says one thing. Paper beats phone.

note_card.text: A WRITTEN DISPUTE STOPS COLLECTION UNTIL VERIFICATION (15 U.S.C. 1692g(b))

scenes.say: There is a federal rule about this. Calling more than seven times in seven days is presumed to be harassment under Regulation F, unless the collector can show otherwise.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: calls in 7 days presumed harassment

scenes.say: You've had nine of them. You don't know that rule yet, so on your lunch break you finally pick up.
A man named Kyle says he's calling for Harborline. He's friendly and he talks fast. He can settle the whole thing today for 400 dollars down.

note_card.text: REG F: MORE THAN 7 CALLS IN 7 DAYS = PRESUMED VIOLATION

scenes.say: In California, a debt collector needs a state license from the Department of Financial Protection and Innovation, which began taking applications in September 2021.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: debt collectors need a DFPI license
visual.source: DFPI – Debt Collection Licensing Act (Fin. Code 100000 et seq.)

scenes.say: California's own collection law, the Rosenthal Act, pulls most of the federal rules in, so the same limits on calls and threats apply under state law too.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: state law adopts the federal FDCPA rules

scenes.say: You tell Kyle you'll think about it and hang up. You write nothing down, and you send nothing in writing.
On day 35 the dispute window closes. Nothing happens that day, which is exactly the problem.

visual.text: the 30-day dispute window closes

scenes.say: Because you only argued on the phone, Harborline never had to stop and prove anything. Dante's line turns out to be a rule.

visual.text: no written dispute, no verification

scenes.say: Level three. The old card.
That night you dig through your old bank app. Your last payment on the Copperleaf card was 55 dollars, back in March 2023.

note_card.text: CA DEBT BUYERS MUST LIST THE DATE OF DEFAULT OR LAST PAYMENT (CIV. CODE 1788.58)

scenes.say: That was the spring the warehouse cut everyone to 28 hours a week. The rent got paid first, and the card got nothing after that.
At that point the balance was about 3,400 dollars. Late fees and interest pushed it to 3,812 by the time the bank stopped expecting you to pay.
A few months later the bank charged the account off. That's an accounting entry. The debt still exists, and the bank is allowed to sell it.

visual.text: written off by the bank, then sold

scenes.say: On your credit report, a collection account can stay for seven years, counted from 180 days after the delinquency began.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: +180 days: how long a collection account can be reported

scenes.say: California gives a creditor four years to sue on a written contract like a card agreement. Once that time runs out, the law says nobody can sue you for it.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: to sue on a written contract

scenes.say: Federal rules say the same thing to the collector. A debt collector must not sue, or threaten to sue, over a time barred debt.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: no lawsuits or threats over expired debt

scenes.say: You count on your fingers. March 2023 to March 2027. You are still inside the window, by about four months.
You're not unusual. Pew researchers found debt cases grew from one in nine civil cases in 1993 to one in four by 2013.

visual.head: PEW RESEARCH
visual.text: civil cases were debt cases by 2013
visual.source: Pew Charitable Trusts, 'How Debt Collectors Are Transforming the Business of State Courts' (2020)

scenes.say: Level four. The summons.
Day 52. A woman in a yellow raincoat is waiting by the mailboxes. She says your full name like a question, and you say yes before you can stop yourself.
She hands you a stack of paper and walks away. The top page is a California summons, form SUM-100, with your name in capital letters.
The summons gives you 30 days after you're served to file a written answer with the court. That clock started the moment you said yes.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: to file a written answer after you're served

scenes.say: Under it is the complaint. Harborline Asset Recovery versus you. They're asking for 4,486 dollars, which is more than 3,812.

visual.text: what Harborline asks the court for

scenes.say: California makes debt buyers spell that out. The balance at charge off, and any interest and fees added after it, have to be stated separately.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: charge-off balance vs. interest and fees added after

scenes.say: The complaint also has to give the date of default or the date of your last payment. Harborline's says March 2023, the month of your 55 dollar payment.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: date of default or last payment must be in the complaint

scenes.say: So it's right there in two lines. 3,812 dollars from the card, and 674 dollars added since the bank let go of it.
Because the amount is under 35,000 dollars, this is a limited civil case in superior court. You expected small claims, and it isn't.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: or less = limited civil case
visual.source: California Courts Self-Help Guide – Civil lawsuits

scenes.say: California doesn't let someone who bought a claim file it in small claims court. So a debt buyer comes to regular court, with a lawyer.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: assignees can't sue in small claims

scenes.say: Level five. The paper trail.
You spread the complaint across the kitchen table. Behind it is a copy of your old card agreement, 31 pages of small print you never read.
California requires a debt buyer to attach the contract, or the document that proves the debt, to the complaint itself.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: the contract goes with the complaint

scenes.say: Page three answers the question from the mailbox. The law makes a debt buyer list every company that bought your debt after the charge off.

note_card.text: DEBT BUYER MUST NAME EVERY BUYER AFTER CHARGE-OFF (CIV. CODE 1788.58)

scenes.say: Copperleaf Bank sold it to a company called Meridian Receivables. Meridian sold it to Harborline. Your old card has had three owners, and you met none of them.
The complaint also has to say that Harborline is the only owner, or has the owners' permission to sue, plus the bank's name and the full account number.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: plus the charge-off creditor and account number

scenes.say: You stare at the list and wonder what a stranger pays for somebody else's old credit card. You'll find out at the very end.
At work you show Dante the stack. He doesn't read it. He taps the top page twice and says it again. Paper beats phone.

note_card.text: DEBT BUYER MUST ATTACH THE CONTRACT (CIV. CODE 1788.58(b))

scenes.say: Level six. The drawer.
Day 60. You look up how to answer. The court's self help site has a form for exactly this, an answer to a contract complaint, PLD-C-010.
Filing it costs money. Under the 2026 statewide fee schedule, a defendant's first paper in a limited case up to 10,000 dollars is 225 dollars.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: to file an answer, limited case up to $10,000
visual.source: Judicial Council – Statewide Civil Fee Schedule, eff. Jan 1, 2026

scenes.say: If you get public benefits, or your household income is under a set limit, you can ask the court to waive that fee with form FW-001.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: request to waive court fees
visual.source: California Courts Self-Help Guide – Fee waivers

scenes.say: The courthouse also has a free self help center where staff explain the forms. You've walked past it twice. Both times you were late for a shift.

note_card.text: FREE COURT SELF-HELP CENTERS EXPLAIN THE FORMS

scenes.say: You check your account. 612 dollars until Friday. You tell yourself you'll deal with the court next week, when things calm down.
The summons goes into the kitchen drawer, on top of Harborline's first letter and the takeout menus.
That's the most common ending for these cases. Pew found courts decided more than 70 percent of debt collection lawsuits by default judgment.

visual.head: PEW RESEARCH
visual.text: of debt collection lawsuits ended in default

scenes.say: Fewer than 10 percent of the people sued in these cases have a lawyer. Most of them go through it alone, or don't show up at all.

visual.text: of defendants have a lawyer

scenes.say: The same report has one more number. In Utah, defendants who had a lawyer won 53 percent of the time, and those without one won 19 percent.

visual.text: Utah: defendants with a lawyer vs. without

scenes.say: Day 70 goes by in the middle of a double shift. Day 82 goes by on a Sunday. The drawer stays closed the whole time.
Level seven. The default.
On day 90, Harborline's lawyer files a request to enter your default. There's no hearing and no phone call, just a form called CIV-100.
The court's own guide says the other side has to wait at least 30 days after you were served. Harborline waited 38.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: days after service before asking for default
visual.source: California Courts Self-Help Guide – Debt lawsuits: default

scenes.say: A California debt buyer can't win a default on its word alone. It needs business records backed by a sworn declaration, plus a copy of the contract.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: business records + contract before a default judgment

scenes.say: Harborline has all of that, because it's the same 31 pages that have been sitting in your kitchen drawer since day 52.

visual.text: the 31-page agreement, exhibit A

scenes.say: A default judgment means the court never heard your side. Anything you might have said about that extra 674 dollars was never said by anyone.

visual.text: never heard by the court

scenes.say: The judgment comes by mail a few weeks later. 4,486 dollars, plus 412 in court costs. 4,898 dollars owed to a company you've never met.
From now on the judgment grows. For a personal credit card judgment under 50,000 dollars, California sets interest at 5 percent a year instead of 10.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: a year on credit card judgments under $50,000

scenes.say: Months later, a clerk at the courthouse self help center tells you about a rule you wish you had heard about sooner.
A court can set aside a default for mistake, surprise or excusable neglect, but you have to ask within a reasonable time, and never more than six months.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: outer limit to ask to set aside a default

scenes.say: You count again. It has been eight months since the default. That door closed while the summons was still in the drawer.
Level eight. The paycheck.
Your supervisor calls you into the office with a sheet of paper. Payroll got an earnings withholding order. Harborline is coming for your wages.
California caps the amount. They can take the lesser of 20 percent of your disposable pay, or 40 percent of what you earn above 48 times the state minimum wage, each week.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: whichever takes less from your weekly pay

scenes.say: In 2026 the California minimum wage is 16.90 an hour. Times 48, that's 811 dollars and 20 cents of weekly pay the formula leaves alone.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: x 48 = $811.20 a week protected by the formula
visual.source: Calif. Dept. of Industrial Relations, news release 2025-118

scenes.say: After taxes your pay is 1,050 dollars a week. 20 percent would be 210. 40 percent of the part above 811 is 95 dollars and 52 cents. The smaller number wins.
Federal law caps garnishment at 25 percent of disposable pay. California's formula takes less here, so it's the one that sets your number.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: federal cap on wage garnishment

scenes.say: Dante sees your face at lunch. You tell him it's 95 dollars a week for about a year. He just nods and hands you half his sandwich.
There's a form for people who can't live on what's left. It's a claim of exemption, WG-006, filed with a financial statement that lists your real bills.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: claim of exemption, with a financial statement
visual.source: California Courts Self-Help Guide – Wage garnishment exemption

scenes.say: You fill it out at the kitchen table, right next to the drawer, and list every bill. Rent alone is 1,640 dollars a month.
Once you file it, the creditor gets 10 days to oppose your claim. Harborline does, and a hearing is set for a Tuesday morning.

visual.text: for the creditor to oppose your claim
visual.source: California Courts Self-Help Guide – Wage garnishment exemption

scenes.say: At the hearing, a commissioner goes through your budget line by line and lowers the weekly amount to 60 dollars. The payments get smaller, and the debt lasts longer.

note_card.text: CLAIM OF EXEMPTION: THE COURT CAN LOWER THE AMOUNT

scenes.say: At 60 dollars a week, 4,898 dollars plus interest takes more than a year and a half of Fridays to pay off.

visual.text: $4,898 at $60 a week, before interest

scenes.say: Level nine. The bank.
Then comes the bank account. One morning your banking app shows a hold on almost everything in checking. Harborline has levied the account.
California protects part of it automatically. For levies from July 1, 2026, the first 2,325 dollars in your account can't be taken.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: protected automatically in a bank account
visual.source: Cal. Code Civ. Proc. 704.220; Judicial Council 2026 adjustment

scenes.say: That number moves with prices. Until the end of June 2026 it was 2,244 dollars, and the Judicial Council raised it this summer to keep up with the cost of living.

visual.text: the protected amount before July 1, 2026
visual.source: Judicial Council of California, June 2026 adjustment

scenes.say: You had 2,610 dollars in there because you were saving for a car. The levy takes 285 of it.

visual.text: what the levy actually takes

scenes.say: If you think more of it should be protected, you file a claim of exemption, form EJ-160, within 15 days if you were served in person, or 20 if by mail.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: to claim an exemption (20 if served by mail)

scenes.say: At the mailboxes, your neighbor Inez from 14C asks if a collector could empty her account too. She lives on her Social Security.
Federal rules give her a shield. When a garnishment order arrives, her bank has to protect two months of directly deposited federal benefits like Social Security.

visual.head: FEDERAL RULE
visual.text: of direct-deposited federal benefits protected

scenes.say: Inez taps your mailbox lid, the one that never closes, and says somebody ought to fix that. You say you will, and then you don't.
Level ten. The long shadow.
Two years later the garnishment is nearly done. You start looking at small condos, and a loan officer pulls your credit report.
A California money judgment can be enforced for 10 years from the day it's entered, and it can be renewed.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: a judgment stays enforceable, renewable

scenes.say: For personal debt judgments under 50,000 dollars, the law now allows that renewal only once, which puts the outside limit at roughly 20 years.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: renewal limit for personal debt under $50,000

scenes.say: And if Harborline records an abstract of the judgment with the county recorder, it becomes a lien on real property you own in that county, for 10 years.

visual.head: CALIFORNIA RULE
visual.text: on real property, for 10 years

scenes.say: The collection account itself has its own clock. It drops off your credit report seven years and 180 days after you first fell behind, somewhere around the fall of 2030.

visual.text: when the collection account leaves your report

scenes.say: The loan officer asks if the judgment is fully paid. You say almost. She says almost is the word that makes underwriters nervous.
So you finish it. You pay the last 340 dollars of the judgment and the interest straight to Harborline's lawyer, and you ask for it in writing.
Two weeks later the paper comes, a filed satisfaction of judgment. You read it twice. For once, you're the one holding the paper.

visual.text: satisfaction of judgment, on paper

scenes.say: One night you add it all up. 3,812 on the card, 674 added before court, 412 in costs, and interest on top, paid out over almost two years of smaller paychecks.
Then you find the answer to the question from page three. The FTC studied debt buyers and found they paid about 4 cents on the dollar, and even less for older debt.

visual.head: FTC STUDY
visual.text: average paid per dollar of debt; older debt sold for less
visual.source: Federal Trade Commission, debt buying study press release, Jan 30, 2013

scenes.say: If Harborline paid that average, your 3,812 dollar card cost them about 152 dollars. You paid them more than thirty times that.
On a Saturday you finally fix the lid on mailbox 14B. It takes one screwdriver and eleven minutes.

note_card.text: FTC 2013: DEBT BUYERS PAID ABOUT 4 CENTS PER DOLLAR

scenes.say: A week later, a new tenant from 14A is standing at the mailboxes holding an envelope from a company she has never heard of.

note_card.text: A COLLECTOR MUST SEND A VALIDATION NOTICE WITHIN 5 DAYS (15 U.S.C. 1692g)

scenes.say: She asks if she should just call them back. You hear yourself say it before you can stop. Paper beats phone, and don't put it in a drawer.

note_card.text: DISPUTE IN WRITING · ANSWER WITHIN 30 DAYS

scenes.say: So tell us honestly. Is there an envelope sitting in a drawer at your place right now that you keep meaning to open?

visual.text: what's in it right now?

seo.title: Your Life at Every Level of Getting Sued by a Debt Collector
seo.title_b: Sued Over a $3,812 Credit Card: Every Level, Letter to Paycheck
seo.hook: An envelope from a company you've never heard of says you owe $3,812. This is every level that follows in California, from the first letter to the day your paycheck shrinks.
seo.summary:
An old credit card you stopped paying in 2023 comes back as an envelope from a debt buyer you've never heard of. This video follows a made-up worker in California through every level of a debt collection lawsuit, in time order: the validation notice and the 30-day written dispute window (FDCPA / Regulation F), the 7-calls-in-7-days rule, California's debt collector license and the Rosenthal Act, the 4-year limit to sue on a written contract and the ban on suing over time-barred debt, the summons (SUM-100) and the 30 days to answer, what a debt buyer's complaint must list under California's Fair Debt Buying Practices Act (charge-off balance, interest and fees added after, every buyer, the contract attached), why debt buyers can't use small claims, the $225 answer fee and the FW-001 fee waiver, what Pew found about default judgments, the 6-month limit to set aside a default, 5% judgment interest on credit card judgments under $50,000, California's wage garnishment formula with the 2026 minimum wage ($16.90 x 48 = $811.20), the $2,325 automatic bank account protection from July 1, 2026, the 2-month protection for federal benefits like Social Security, how long a judgment lasts and when a collection account leaves a credit report, and what the FTC found debt buyers pay per dollar.

Everyone in this story is made up, and so are the story's dollar amounts (the $3,812 balance, the $674 add-on, court costs, pay, rent and savings). Copperleaf Bank, Meridian Receivables and Harborline Asset Recovery are fictional names. The rules, deadlines and statistics come from the sources listed below. Real cases depend on the facts, the court and the county.

Chapters: see the chapter list (Level 1: The letter ... Level 10: The long shadow, The end: What it cost).
seo.disclaimer: This video explains general California and federal rules for education and entertainment. It is not legal advice. Debt collection rules differ by state and change over time, and dollar amounts are adjusted regularly. If you have received a collection letter, a summons or a garnishment order, contact your court's self-help center, a legal aid office or a licensed attorney.

Kanalen 28 d (TITTARTID_REGLER 23 nov): 663 exponeringar, 3,8 % CTR, 4:37 snitt – DAC har kanalernas bästa tittartid men minst räckvidd. Fortkörningsmanuset dac-2026-11-23 (Every Level-titeln) är skrivet men inte publicerat.
forbattring.problem: Krockvideon hade bra struktur men titeln var en egen frågeformulering med liten sökvolym och bilderna var den gamla platta Skia-stilen. DAC:s räckvidd (663 exponeringar på 28 dagar) är för liten för att nå 4 000 timmar – ämnet måste vara något väldigt många råkar ut för och titeln en mall som YouTube redan sprider.
forbattring.andring: FORMAT_BLUEPRINT (ägarorder 23/11, stilen godkänd 24/11 10:47): trendtiteln 'Your Life at Every Level of …' ordagrant + ett av de vanligaste civilmålen i USA (Pew: 1 av 4 civilmål är skuldmål, över 70 % slutar med tredskodom). 10 nivåkort 'LEVEL ONE / THE LETTER' … 'LEVEL TEN / THE LONG SHADOW' i den godkända svarta PatrickHand-stilen, siffer-bubblor (real/label) med en verklig regel eller statistik i snitt var ~13:e sekund (största lucka ≈30 s), andra person från första meningen, halvrealistisk vuxen huvudperson (grå henley). Ny delstat (Kalifornien) och nytt rättsområde (skuldindrivning, utmätning) jämfört med Florida-krocken och Kalifornien-boten.
forbattring.forvantat: CTR ≥ 4 % (trendtiteln + nivåminiatyren), ≥ 55 % kvar vid 0:30, ≥ 35 % vid 2:00, snittvisning ≥ 5:00; fler exponeringar från 'Browse' via titelmallen som 9+ kanaler publicerar denna vecka.
forbattring.referens: Trendens vinnare: Honest Life POV 'Your Life at Every Level of Living Off the Grid' (678 751 visningar senaste månaden, 27:38, FORMAT_BLUEPRINT – bildrutor 0:01–15:00 tagna i ägarens Chrome 23/11) + veckans juridiska variant 'How Getting Arrested on a Cruise Ship Destroys Your Life at Every Level' (Miles Unnoticed, 11 694 visningar/vecka, TREND_2026-11-24). Transkript kunde inte hämtas i denna körning: ingen Chrome i molnkörningen (youtube-transcriber kräver den), YouTube nås inte från molnet (proxy 403 enligt TREND-filen), vidIQ 3 krediter. Kroken 0/5/10/20/30 s enligt blueprinten: 0 s nivån direkt ('Level One, The Tent.'), ~5 s en sinnesdetalj i du-form i en varm miljö, ~10 s första verkliga kostnaden i en siffer-bubbla ('SAVINGS: $38,000'), ~20 s insatsen för hela livet, ~30 s övergång till nästa nivå. Webbsök 24/11: ingen video heter 'Your Life at Every Level of Getting Sued (by a Debt Collector)'; närmast 'Your Life At Every Level Of Getting Out Of Debt' (UTs5htKgWjI, annat ämne) och tipsvideor som 'Getting Sued By A Debt Collector? DO THIS FIRST!'.
forbattring.vi_slår_den_med: Hotet syns i första bilden (kuvertet i lucka 14B) i stället för en lugn miljöbild, 30 öppnade källor med paragrafnummer på skärmen (Reg F, Civ. Code 1788.58/1788.60, CCP 706.050 med 2026 års minimilön, $2 325-skyddet från 1 juli 2026), en uträkning tittaren kan göra på sin egen lön ($16.90 × 48 = $811.20), och en gåta som betalas av en verklig siffra (FTC: ~4 cent per dollar → Harborline betalade ~152 dollar för ditt kort).

hooks_kandidater.A_vald: Mailbox 14B has never closed right. Tonight an envelope is sticking out of it. / It says you owe 3,812 dollars, and it gives you 30 days… (mekanism: specificity + stakes; bilden = miniatyren direkt; fungerar utan ljud tack vare $3,812 på brevet)
hooks_kandidater.B: The company suing you paid about 4 cents for every dollar it says you owe. (curiosity gap/dissonans – men första bilden blir ett kort, inte miniatyrens scen, och den största payoffen avslöjas direkt)
hooks_kandidater.C: Seven out of ten people sued over a debt never answer, and they lose without a hearing. (identitet/statistik – stark men abstrakt, ingen person i bild de första sekunderna)
hooks_kandidater.val: A – miniatyrens scen från bildruta 0, insats med siffra inom 5 s, löftet i klartext vid ~10 s; B:s gåta används som löfte vid ~22 s och betalas i slutet, C:s statistik kommer i nivå 6.

standard_check.miniatyr: FORMAT_BLUEPRINT DAC (godkänd 24/11): 'LEVEL 1' vit + gul undertitel '$3,812' över scenen, halvrealistisk man med kuvertet (TREND-filens förslag); MINIATYR_REGLER 0: hjälten ≈60 % av höjden i höger tredjedel, en textrad, 3 ord, ljus varm miljö; B = annan bild (lönespecen på lastkajen, LEVEL 8), C = annan bild (kökslådan, fråga '30 DAYS?').
standard_check.krok: andra person från första meningen; plats + insats (lucka 14B, $3,812, 30 dagar) inom 10 s; löftet i klartext vid ~10 s ('from this envelope to your paycheck'); gåta (vem är Harborline? vad betalade de?) vid 16 och 28 s; första verkliga regeln (5 dagar, 1692g) vid ~33 s.
standard_check.nivåer: 10 nivåer + slut: The letter, The calls, The old card, The summons, The paper trail, The drawer, The default, The paycheck, The bank, The long shadow, What it cost; varje nivå: första ögonblick → det svåraste → verklig regel med källa (real-kort) → insidersanning → känsloslag → övergång.
standard_check.motiv: brevlåda 14B vars lock aldrig stänger (0:00, nivå 4, nivå 9, slutet när du lagar den) + kökslådan med hämtmatsmenyerna (nivå 1, 6, 7, 8, slutfrågan) + Dantes replik 'Paper beats phone' (nivå 2, 5, 8 – blir en verklig regel i nivå 2 och din egen replik i slutet).
standard_check.slut: cykeln: en ny granne i 14A står vid brevlådorna med ett kuvert från ett företag hon aldrig hört talas om; du säger Dantes replik; fäst fråga till tittaren om kuvertet i lådan.
standard_check.källor: 31 källor i beskrivningen (federal lag, CFR, Kaliforniens lagar, Judicial Council, domstolarnas självhjälpssidor, DFPI, DIR, Pew, FTC); källrad på varje real-kort.
standard_check.miljöer: mailroom (ny), apartment, loading_dock, collector_office, self_help_center (ny), court_hall, courtroom, bank – tom miljö först i nivå 7 (court_hall).
standard_check.tittartid: första 30 s: 4 helbildsscener med walk_to + 2 kort, ingen medium/närbild, ingen presentation de första 12 s, byte var ~5 s, slutlöfte vid ~10 s och ~25 s.

notes.påhittat: alla personer (du, Dante, Kyle, Inez, processdelgivaren, expediten, kommissionären, lånehandläggaren, den nya grannen), företagen Copperleaf Bank, Meridian Receivables och Harborline Asset Recovery, numret 916, alla belopp i berättelsen ($3,812, $3,400, $674, $4,486, $412 i rättegångskostnader, $4,898, $55, $400, $612,40, lön $1,050/v, $60/v efter förhandlingen, hyra $1,640, $2,610 på kontot, $340 sista betalningen), dagarna 9/35/52/60/70/82/90, 31 sidor, 28 timmar, 22 år, 11 minuter.
notes.uträkningar: $3,812 + $674 = $4,486; + $412 = $4,898; 48 × $16.90 = $811.20; $1,050 × 20 % = $210; ($1,050 − $811.20) × 40 % = $95.52 → lägst = $95.52; $4,898 / $95.52 ≈ 51 veckor ≈ 1 år; $4,898 / $60 ≈ 82 veckor ≈ 1,6 år; $2,610 − $2,325 = $285; 4 % × $3,812 = $152.48 ≈ $152; $4,898 / $152 ≈ 32 → 'more than thirty times'; dag 90 − dag 52 = 38; dispute window: brevet dag 1 + 5 arbetsdagar + 30 dagar ≈ dag 35+ (förenklat 'day 35'); preskription: sista betalning mars 2023 + 4 år = mars 2027 (förenklat – i praktiken räknas fristen från kontraktsbrottet/första missade betalningen); FCRA: försenad från ca april 2023 + 180 dagar + 7 år ≈ hösten 2030.
notes.osäkert: Kaliforniens lagtexter lästes på california.public.law/FindLaw (inofficiella speglar) eftersom leginfo gav fel – CCP 685.010 lästes på leginfo. 'Two years later … roughly 20 years at most' (683.110(c) förnyelse bara en gång) är förenklat. Lokala minimilöner högre än $16,90 gäller i vissa städer (706.050 använder den högre) – berättelsen anger ingen stad. 'Federal rules give her a shield … two months' – 31 CFR 212 gäller när banken får ett utmätningsbeslut och förmånen satts in direkt; vi säger 'when a garnishment order arrives'. Att kommissionären sänker beloppet till $60 är berättelse (domstolen KAN sänka). FTC:s 4 cent är ett genomsnitt från 2013 – videon säger 'if Harborline paid that average'. Pews siffror är från 2020 års rapport (data 1993–2013 och senare stickprov). Satisfaction of judgment: berättelse, ingen paragraf citeras.
